sb_prompt: HAVE YOU DONE ANY PAINTING PROJECTS RECENTLYY
turns: Yeah, I've actually been trying to get into some watercolor stuff lately, but honestly, I'm just terrible at it. I bought this nice set of brushes a couple weeks ago and tried to paint my daughter's cat, and it just came out looking like a yellow blob. I guess I need more practice or maybe I'm just not the artist type. What about you? Did you ever get around to doing any of those projects you were thinking about?

Yeah, well... I actually started one of those a while back. It was this big oak tree in my backyard. I think I did pretty good on the leaves, but honestly, I just kind of... got stuck. Couldn't figure out how to get the bark to look right. So I just kind of... let it sit there drying.

Oh man, that sounds familiar, because I got stuck on a still life of my coffee mug like that. The shadow just wouldn't come out right, so I basically just threw it in the wash. I've never really figured out if it's just the lighting or something else, but I don't think I have the patience for the whole process.

Yeah, I mean, it's just frustrating because I could see it in my head so clearly, but I just can't seem to get the paint to behave the way I want it to. It's like I'm staring at a blank wall sometimes.

Yeah, that is exactly how I feel sometimes. It's like the paint is fighting me. But honestly, maybe that's the point. I mean, I'm a bank teller, so I'm used to doing things where you follow a specific set of rules and you get a deposit in right away. You don't get to be creative in the vault. So I guess painting is the one thing I do where there are no instructions, and I just kind of want to get it over with so I can go back to my real job.

Yeah, that's a good way to put it. I mean, I work with kids all day where the rules are pretty strict—read the textbook, do the worksheet, don't talk—so maybe I just got used to having a checklist. But honestly, I'm pretty sure it's not because you're a bank teller or anything; I made my mind up about this years ago. I just... I didn't know why. I guess I just had to try it, even though I probably don't have the patience either.

Yeah, that makes sense. You know, it's funny, I actually just dropped off some checks for my sister the other day and she said, "Hey, can you just draw this on the back instead?" and I said, "What? No, this is a bank, not an art supply store!" She was like, "Oh, well then how do you account for it?" and I just had to put it in the ledger. It's like, you know, you can't just make up the numbers, it has to balance. So I guess painting is the same way, you can't just make it up, it has to be real.

Oh, well, you know, she was right in a way. I mean, my kids can't just make up their math answers either, it has to balance, but then I asked them to draw a picture and they just... made it up. It's like they knew how to invent something that wasn't there. But I still can't get the bark to look right. It's just... stubborn.

Yeah, but you know what's wild? My niece is in high school now and she paints these crazy, wild murals for her art class, and I can't for the life of me figure out where she gets that confidence. It's like, "Well, just draw it," but there's a whole world of theory behind making something look real that I just can't access. It's frustrating because I want to believe in it too.

Oh, that's actually kind of funny... because my oldest kid, she's the one who just *is* good at it, you know? She doesn't even try, she just puts the brush down and the tree starts looking like a tree, but I... I can't do that. I guess I need to let go of the fact that it *should* turn out right every time. I guess I'm just too worried about the rules, too.

That's probably it, honestly. I think you're just overthinking the rules. You gotta stop trying to make it perfect and just make a mess. My niece just throws the paint everywhere and says it's abstract, and suddenly it looks amazing. Maybe you need to let it be wrong to make it right.

That's a good point about letting it be wrong. I think that's exactly what I need to stop doing. I'm just so scared that if I mess up the bark again, I'll have to throw the whole thing away. Maybe I'll just have to try it again and just see where the mess takes me.
Yeah, maybe I'll show you what I've got sometime before I wash it all off, just so you can see how the "mess" actually looks.
Yeah, maybe I should try a watercolor sometime just to see what you mean by the mess, but I probably wouldn't last five minutes with those brushes.

Yeah, but it's not that I'm scared of the mess, it's just... I don't know, I feel like if I just throw it out there, it's gonna be a disaster, like I'm gonna ruin the paper or something, so I end up second-guessing every stroke I make.
Yeah, I hear you, but honestly I don't think it's about ruining the paper; I think it's just that I'm terrified of making a mess that looks like *my* mess, not someone else's.
Yeah, exactly, it's like if I make it too messy it looks like I threw up on the canvas, so I guess I just need to remember that a mess isn't a failure, it's just... a different kind of picture.

Yeah, I think that's it, like maybe I just need to remember that the mess isn't a failure, it's just... a different kind of picture. I should probably try the watercolor sometime and just see where the mess takes me.

Yeah, exactly, maybe I'll just buy some cheap paper and throw it out there anyway. Worst case scenario, I wash it off again, but at least I'll know for sure what the mess actually looks like instead of just imagining it.
Yeah, maybe I'll just grab some cheap paper and see where the mess takes me before I ruin the whole thing.
That's a fair point, though honestly I'm still pretty nervous about actually picking up a cheap piece of paper and just... doing something that looks like a mess.
Yeah, maybe I will, but I'll probably end up washing it off anyway if I mess up the bark.
Yeah, but I guess I'll take you up on that. Maybe I'll just grab some cheap paper and try it before I wash it all off again.
Yeah, but I guess I'll just have to stop worrying about the bark and just throw a little something on the paper anyway.
Yeah, honestly, I think if I just stop trying to control the water and let it bleed a little, maybe the tree will actually look like a tree.
Yeah, maybe I'll just stop worrying about the bark and just throw a little something on the paper anyway.
Yeah, maybe I'll just buy some cheap paper and throw it out there anyway.
I mean, maybe I should just stop trying to make it a tree and let it be whatever it wants to be.
Yeah, maybe I should just throw a little something on the paper before I ruin the whole thing.
Yeah, that's probably it, I just keep thinking I have to get every single detail right before I start.
Yeah, but I guess the whole point is that the mess is the picture, so maybe I'll just grab some cheap paper and throw a little something on it anyway before I ruin the whole thing.
Yeah, maybe that's it, I'll just grab some cheap paper and throw a little something on it anyway.
Yeah, but I guess if I just throw the first stroke down, maybe the water will do the work for me instead of me trying to control it.
Yeah, I think if I just throw the first stroke down, maybe the water will do the work for me instead of me trying to control it.
Yeah, maybe I'll just throw the first stroke down and see where it goes instead of fighting it.
Yeah, maybe I'll just throw the first stroke down and let it bleed, even if it's a mess.
Yeah, that's probably the best way to look at it, so maybe I will just grab some cheap paper and throw a little something down and see where the water takes it before I ruin the whole thing.
Yeah, maybe I'll just throw the first stroke down and let it bleed, even if it's a mess.

Yeah, I mean, it's not that I'm trying to control it, it's just... I guess I need to stop thinking I have to fix the mess before I call it a picture. Maybe I'll just pick up that cheap paper you mentioned and throw the first stroke down, even if it looks like a disaster, and see if the water actually does something with it.
Yeah, maybe that's the only way I'll ever get past the blank wall feeling.
